answer.location_description: Small 3x3 square near the top-left corner of the image, at rows 1-3 and columns 1-3.
answer.mechanism: Layer-1 units that detect a large blob (1, 7, 11, 12, 14, 16, 19) carry strong positive weights (about +60 to +99) on the 3x3 top-left patch. Layer-1 units that detect a small blob (3, 5, 8, 10, 17, 20, 23, 25, 30, 31) carry strong negative weights (about -50 to -99) on the same patch. In layer 2, the large-blob units feed u13 (output weight +99) and u8 (+65). The small-blob units feed u9 (-98), u3 (-94) and u0 (-80). A bright patch therefore turns up the class-1 pathway and turns down the class-0 pathway, which pushes the logit positive.
answer.evidence: The 3x3 block at r1-r3, c1-c3 stands out sharply from its neighbours in about 17 of the 32 hidden units. Examples: unit 1 has 66 59 98 / 59 96 71 / 70 88 66 there, against roughly ±30 noise around it. Unit 16 has 83 99 97 ... and unit 3 has -91 -78 -84 / -84 -68 -58 / -77 -94 -71. The surrounding border pixels in these units carry no comparable structure. In every unit the sign of the patch weights matches the unit's blob-size role, positive for large-blob units and negative for small-blob units. The layer-2 routing then sends this toward class 1: u13 takes 48, 87, 63, 68, 78 from units 1, 7, 12, 14, 19 and -78, -76, -92, -87 from units 5, 8, 17, 25. u9 takes 74, 85, 90, 77 from units 3, 5, 17, 23.
answer.main_feature: Blob size is read from radial structure around the centre. Large-blob units respond positively over a wide disc or annulus (roughly rows 5-18, cols 5-18). Small-blob units respond positively to a bright small centre and negatively to a surrounding ring (rows 6-17), so they fire when that ring is dark.
